decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet shelf display builds directly on the firm's core cardboard display knowledge, so in-house R&D lets it interpret results and refine the product cheaply.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a close variant of the established offer and fits the firm's existing design and production competence, so it is worth retaining.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is central to the firm's display know-how and production capacity, which makes it a low-risk product to keep.
The eighth-pallet display extends the core pallet-display range using existing knowledge and equipment, so it remains a sensible part of the portfolio.

The wooden pallet draws on a material outside the firm's core paper competence, which limits its absorptive capacity, but it complements the display offer, so it is kept for now with a higher risk of being dropped.
The media-product display is technically close to the core offer, but demand for physical media is shrinking, which raises its drop risk, though it is still kept.
